title: Coherent formal modules Coh(X, I), the completion functor, and systems with support proper over a base
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals (the ideal sheaf of a closed subscheme [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]). $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ denotes the full subcategory of the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose objects are the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. (0) (Notation.) For a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ is the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] (the subsheaf generated by the local sections $as$, $a$ a local section of $\mathcal J$, $s$ of $\mathcal F$); $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$; $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ is the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal J\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$. (1) $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the category whose objects are inverse systems $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge1}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\mathcal O_X$-linear transition maps $\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ such that $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ and the transition map induces an isomorphism $\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$, for every $n\ge1$; a morphism $(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ is a family of $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\alpha_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_n$ commuting with the transition maps. (2) The *completion functor* $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ sends a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ to $\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)_{n\ge1}$ with the canonical surjections as transition maps, and an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ to $u^\wedge=(u\bmod\mathcal I^n)_n$. (3) For a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, an object $(\mathcal F_n)$ is *annihilated by $\mathcal K$* if $\mathcal K\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$; it is *annihilated by a power of $\mathcal I$* ($\mathcal I$-power torsion) if it is annihilated by $\mathcal I^c$ for some $c\ge1$, which holds if and only if the transition maps $\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_c$ are isomorphisms for all $n\ge c$ (Stacks' formulation); for a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z$, $(\mathcal F_n)$ is *supported on $Z$* if it is annihilated by $\mathcal I_Z$ (likewise a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ is supported on $Z$ if $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$). (4) If moreover $f:X\to S$ is a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$ is the full subcategory of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ of the objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ (a closed subset of $X$) is proper over $S$, and $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(\mathcal O_X)$ is the full subcategory of $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ of the coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with support proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; since $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal I\mathcal F)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, the completion functor maps the second subcategory into the first.

proof.text: Source plan retained for the three existing open theorems; these steps are not yet formalized by this delivery. (The product $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and the powers $\mathcal J^n$.) Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. The tensor product $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is quasi-coherent and for every affine open $U$ its sections are $\mathcal J(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal F(U)$ via the sheafification map $t_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]. The maps $\mathcal J(V)\otimes\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal F(V)$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$, are $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear and compatible with restriction, so form a map of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, which factors uniquely through the sheafification: this is the multiplication $\mu:\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$. Its image $\mathcal J\mathcal F=\operatorname{Im}\mu$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal F$, and for $U$ affine $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)=\mu_U(\mathcal J(U)\otimes\mathcal F(U))=\mathcal J(U)\mathcal F(U)$, the submodule generated by the products [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image, part (1)-(3)]; by the definition of $\operatorname{Im}$ there, $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ consists of the sections locally of the form $\sum a_is_i$, i.e. it is the subsheaf generated by the products. Taking $\mathcal F=\mathcal J^{n}$ (quasi-coherent by induction) gives the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n\subseteq\mathcal J^n\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, and by induction $\mathcal J^n(U)=\mathcal J(U)^n$ for $U$ affine. (Stacks describes $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ in exactly this way, as the image of $\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, in the proof of Lemma 01YP.)

proof.text: Source plan retained for the three existing open theorems; these steps are not yet formalized by this delivery. (Computing on affine opens.) The affine opens of $X$ form a basis of the topology, and a sheaf is determined by its sections on a basis: two subsheaves of $\mathcal F$ with the same sections on every affine open are equal (a section over any open $W$ lies in a subsheaf iff its restrictions to an affine cover of $W$ do), and a morphism of sheaves that is bijective on every affine open is an isomorphism. With step 1 this gives, for quasi-coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal J,\mathcal J'$ and $a,b\ge1$: (a) an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ maps $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ into $\mathcal J\mathcal G$ (on affine $U$, $u_U(\sum a_is_i)=\sum a_iu_U(s_i)$); (b) $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal J'$ implies $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal J'\mathcal F$, in particular $\mathcal J^{a+1}\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal J^a\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal J^b\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal J^a\mathcal F$ for $b\ge a$; (c) $\mathcal J^a(\mathcal J^b\mathcal F)=\mathcal J^{a+b}\mathcal F$ (on affine $U$, $J^a(J^bM)=J^{a+b}M$ for $J=\mathcal J(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$).

proof.text: Source plan retained for the three existing open theorems; these steps are not yet formalized by this delivery. (The quotient $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ is coherent.) Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent. As $X$ is locally Noetherian, $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The cokernel $q:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ of the inclusion of the quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ (step 1) is quasi-coherent, $q$ is an epimorphism of sheaves with kernel $\mathcal J\mathcal F$, and on affine $U$, $(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(U)/\mathcal J(U)\mathcal F(U)$ with $q_U$ the quotient map [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. It is of finite type: if $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal F|_U$ is surjective (as a map of sheaves) on an open $U$, so is its composite with the surjection $q|_U$. Hence $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. As a cokernel it has the universal property: an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ with $v(\mathcal J\mathcal F)=0$ factors uniquely as $\bar v\circ q$.

proof.text: ($\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is well defined and is a category.) For an inverse system of coherent modules with $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$, the transition map $t_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ maps $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}$ into $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ (step 2(a)), so by step 3 it induces a unique $\bar t_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\bar t_n\circ q=t_n$; condition (1) asks that $\bar t_n$ be an isomorphism, which is meaningful. Morphisms are families $(\alpha_n)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps with $t^{\mathcal G}_n\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_nt^{\mathcal F}_n$; the identity family is one, and if $(\alpha_n)$, $(\beta_n)$ are, then $t_n\beta_{n+1}\alpha_{n+1}=\beta_nt_n\alpha_{n+1}=\beta_n\alpha_nt_n$, so the componentwise composite is one. Associativity and the unit laws hold componentwise, and $\operatorname{Hom}$ is a subset of $\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F_n,\mathcal G_n)$. So $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is a category (Stacks: 'a morphism of such inverse systems is defined as usual'); it is the full subcategory of the category of inverse systems of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the objects satisfying (1). (That it is abelian is the separate node lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian, Lemma 087X, not part of the definition.)

proof.text: Source plan retained for the three existing open theorems; these steps are not yet formalized by this delivery. ($\mathcal F^\wedge$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$.) Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent and $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$, coherent by step 3, with $q_n:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F_n$. As $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ (step 2(b)), $q_n$ kills $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F$ and factors uniquely as $p_n\circ q_{n+1}$ with $p_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ (step 3), surjective since $q_n$ is; these are the canonical transition maps. On an affine open $U$, with $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $I=\mathcal I(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$, step 1 and step 3 give $\mathcal F_n(U)=M/I^nM$, $p_{n,U}$ the canonical map, $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n)(U)=I^n(M/I^nM)=0$, and $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1})(U)=I^n(M/I^{n+1}M)=I^nM/I^{n+1}M$, so the induced map $(\mathcal F_{n+1}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+1})(U)=(M/I^{n+1}M)/(I^nM/I^{n+1}M)\to M/I^nM$ is bijective (third isomorphism theorem). By step 2, $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ and $\bar p_n$ is an isomorphism. So $\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F_n,p_n)$ satisfies (1).

proof.text: (The completion functor is a functor.) For $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ between coherent modules, $q^{\mathcal G}_n\circ u$ kills $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ since $u(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$ (step 2(a)), so there is a unique $u_n:\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\to\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n\mathcal G$ with $u_nq^{\mathcal F}_n=q^{\mathcal G}_nu$ (step 3). Then $p^{\mathcal G}_nu_{n+1}$ and $u_np^{\mathcal F}_n$ both composed with the epimorphism $q^{\mathcal F}_{n+1}$ give $q^{\mathcal G}_nu$, hence are equal; so $u^\wedge=(u_n)$ is a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ (step 4). By the uniqueness in step 3, $(\mathrm{id})^\wedge=\mathrm{id}$ and $(vu)^\wedge=v^\wedge u^\wedge$ (both $v_nu_n$ and $(vu)_n$ satisfy the defining identity). So (2) defines a functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. (Its exactness, Lemma 0881, and full faithfulness in the proper case, Lemma 0883, are statements of their own, not part of the definition.) Lean realization: formalModuleQuotientMap_id and formalModuleQuotientMap_comp cancel the cokernel projection and simplify cokernel.π_desc. formalCompletionSystem_laws, formalCompletionMap_naturality and formalCompletionMap_laws follow from these two identities and componentwise equality. The factorization proof formalModuleQuotient_map_zero remains open; no new theorem is introduced.

Source plan retained for the three existing open theorems; these steps are not yet formalized by this delivery. (Annihilation and support, part (3).) These are definitions: $\mathcal K\mathcal F_n$ is defined by step 1, and an object annihilated by $\mathcal K$ is one with $\mathcal K\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$; 'supported on $Z$' is the case $\mathcal K=\mathcal I_Z$, quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Stacks (paragraph before Lemma 0889) defines '$(\mathcal F_n)$ is annihilated by $\mathcal I^c$' as: $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F_c$ for $n\ge c$ (via the transition maps). Equivalence with $\mathcal I^c\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$: on an affine open $U$ write $M_n=\mathcal F_n(U)$, $I=\mathcal I(U)$; by condition (1) and steps 1-3, $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is surjective with kernel $I^nM_{n+1}$. By induction on $n\ge c$ the composite $\tau:M_n\to M_c$ is surjective with kernel $I^cM_n$: for $n>c$, $M_n\to M_{n-1}$ is surjective with kernel $I^{n-1}M_n\subseteq I^cM_n$, and the preimage of $I^cM_{n-1}$ (the kernel of $M_{n-1}\to M_c$) under it is $I^cM_n+I^{n-1}M_n=I^cM_n$. Hence $\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_c$ induces $\mathcal F_n/\mathcal I^c\mathcal F_n\cong\mathcal F_c$ (step 2). If $\mathcal I^c\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n$, the transition maps $\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_c$ ($n\ge c$) are isomorphisms. Conversely if they are, $\mathcal I^c\mathcal F_n=0$ for $n\ge c$, and for $n<c$, $\mathcal I^c\mathcal F_n\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_n=0$ (step 2(b)). (That a coherent module supported on $Z$ is $i_*$ of a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module, which Stacks calls equivalent in the proof of Theorem 088E, is Lemma 087T, the node lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence; it is not used by the definition.)
